Sister Amaranth has made the poisons milder and the hourglass shorter.|The antidote race. You can smell three of Sister Amaranth's poisons from the door now; she has started using a fourth.} {The last pair to finish washes everyone's beakers.|One pair's tongues are already blue.|{season == "summer": The heat makes everything evaporate twice as fast.|Rain hammers the windows and nobody can hear the hourglass.}} Identify it by testing {Three reagents and one colour change say hiccup-root. You counter it with mint and pepper and drink both before the sand's half gone. "Keep doing that," says Sister Amaranth.|You name it in two tests and brew the counter nearly blindfold. Sister Amaranth watches you drink without a word, which is praise.|You identify the fourth poison, the one she thought nobody would get. She looks at you over the hourglass and adds a fifth to her list.} {You guess wrong and drink a counter to the wrong thing. Your tongue is blue until supper.|You run out of sand, drink your best guess and hiccup in iambic rhythm for an hour.|Your antidote works on everything except the poison. Sister Amaranth hands you a second one, the right one, without comment.} Brew a broad remedy instead {You skip the testing and brew a remedy that counters most mild poisons, expensively. It works; it takes a lot out of you.|A broad remedy, slow and draining, and very safe. Sister Amaranth notes it as "a cautious answer", which is not praise.|Your broad remedy is so reliable now that the other pairs come to borrow it. Brewing it still leaves you hollow.}
